output.title: Design against untested assumptions by narrowing the decision
output.body:
If you want to design against untested assumptions, start by narrowing the decision. For a small business owner, the real question is usually not “can AI do this?” It is: which recurring workflow is frequent enough, measurable enough, and already digital enough to justify a bounded pilot instead of more manual work or another hire.

That is where untested assumptions hide. A demo can look fine and still miss the live questions: who approves what, what data is actually available, and how much handover effort the workflow needs. Human approval still has to stay in place for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

Bareni’s working rule is simple: work inside the customer’s environment, keep the setup in the customer’s name from the start, and hand over finished code on delivery. That is policy and no-lock-in positioning, not a warranty.

One practical next step is to write down one recurring workflow and note three things: how often it happens, what measurable outcome it should affect, and where the approval point sits. If those are still vague, the assumption is still doing the work for you.
